title: CornerNet-Lite: Efficient Keypoint Based Object Detection

problem.summary: CornerNet reaches state-of-the-art one-stage accuracy but at about 1.1s per image, too slow for video or interactive use; simply processing fewer pixels or a smaller resolution destroys its accuracy, so an efficient keypoint-based detector is needed.
statements: CornerNet costs 1.1s per image (42.2% AP on COCO), which is too slow for real-time or interactive video applications.
Reducing input resolution and test scales speeds CornerNet to 42ms but drops AP to 25.6%, far below YOLOv3's 33.0%.
Detector efficiency must be attacked along two axes: the number of pixels processed and the amount of processing per pixel.

evidence.quote: However, this accuracy comes at high processing cost.
However, a major drawback of CornerNet is its inference speed.
It achieves an average precision (AP) of 42.2% on COCO at an inference cost of 1.1s per image
but would decrease the AP to 25.6% which is much lower than YOLOv3's 33.0%.

background.summary: The paper builds on CornerNet's corner-keypoint detector with a stacked hourglass backbone, on the saccade/cascade line of selective-crop inference (R-CNN variants, AutoFocus), and on efficient architecture design (SqueezeNet fire modules, MobileNet depth-wise separable convolutions); the gap is that no prior work made keypoint-based detection efficient.

relatedWork.name: CornerNet
relatedWork.relation: the accurate but slow baseline being optimized
relatedWork.quote: CornerNet [27], the state-of-the-art among them, detects and groups the top-left and bottom-right corners of bounding boxes;

relatedWork.name: AutoFocus
relatedWork.relation: prior saccade-style method whose crops are multi-type and mixed rather than single-type and multi-object
relatedWork.quote: In contrast, CornerNet-Saccade produces multiple detections per crop with a single-stage network.

relatedWork.name: SqueezeNet
relatedWork.relation: source of the fire module design used in CornerNet-Squeeze
relatedWork.quote: SqueezeNet [20] proposes a fire module to reduce the number of parameters in AlexNet [25] by 50x, while achieving similar performance.

relatedWork.name: MobileNets
relatedWork.relation: source of depth-wise separable convolutions for the compact backbone
relatedWork.quote: MobileNets [16] are a class of lightweight networks that use depth-wise separable convolutions [6], and proposes strategies to achieve a good trade-off between accuracy and latency.

evidence.quote: There has been a long history of using saccades [12, 42, 63] in object detection to speed up inference.
The efficiency of ConvNets is important to many mobile and embedded applications.

solution.summary: CornerNet-Lite combines two variants: CornerNet-Saccade predicts attention maps on a downsized image and only processes high-resolution crops at promising locations, while CornerNet-Squeeze replaces the heavy hourglass with a compact backbone built from fire modules and depth-wise separable convolutions.
solution.approach: Cut pixels processed with saccade-style attention-driven crops and cut per-pixel cost with a SqueezeNet/MobileNet-inspired compact hourglass backbone.
components: three scale-specific attention maps predicted on 255/192-pixel downsized images
zoom-in crop processing (ss=4, sm=2, sl=1) with Soft-NMS merging and boundary-box removal
Hourglass-54 backbone (3 modules, 54 layers) for CornerNet-Saccade
fire modules plus depth-wise separable convolutions in CornerNet-Squeeze

evidence.quote: CornerNet-Saccade, which uses an attention mechanism to eliminate the need for exhaustively processing all pixels of the image, and CornerNet-Squeeze, which introduces a new compact backbone architecture.
CornerNet-Saccade speeds up inference by reducing the number of pixels to process.
CornerNet-Squeeze speeds up inference by reducing the amount of processing per pixel.

It incorporates ideas from SqueezeNet [20] and MobileNets [16], and introduces a new, compact hourglass backbone that makes extensive use of 1×1 convolution, bottleneck layer, and depth-wise separable convolution.

experiments.summary: All detectors are timed on the same 1080Ti/i7-7700k machine on COCO; the paper reports accuracy-speed points for both variants, ablates Hourglass-54 vs Hourglass-104 and each Squeeze modification, and tests the failed Squeeze+Saccade combination.

evidence.quote: CornerNet-Saccade is suitable for offline processing, improving the efficiency of CornerNet by 6.0x and the AP by 1.0% on COCO.
(34.4% AP at 30ms for CornerNet-Squeeze compared to 33.0% AP at 39ms for YOLOv3 on COCO).
CornerNet-Squeeze is faster and more accurate than YOLOv3. CornerNet-Saccade is more accurate than CornerNet at multi-scales and 6 times faster.

limitations.summary: The two variants cover opposite corners of the accuracy-efficiency tradeoff but cannot be combined: Squeeze+Saccade is slower and less accurate than Squeeze alone, and the compact backbone is too weak to predict good attention maps.
items: Combining both tricks fails: CornerNet-Squeeze-Saccade is slower and less accurate than CornerNet-Squeeze.
The ultra-compact backbone lacks the capacity to detect objects and predict attention maps at the same time.
CornerNet-Squeeze operates on a single image scale, leaving little room for saccade-based savings, and its small-object AP (13.7) trails YOLOv3 (18.3) on COCO test.

evidence.quote: This is because for saccades to help, the network needs to be able to generate sufficiently accurate attention maps, but the ultra-compact architecture of CornerNet-Squeeze does not have this extra capacity.
Due to its ultra-compact architecture, CornerNetSqueeze-Saccade does not have enough capacity to detect objects and predict attention maps simultaneously.
The results in Tab. 5 suggest that saccade can only help if the attention maps are sufficiently accurate.

applications.detail: the original CornerNet's latency is described as too slow for video applications needing real-time or interactive rates, which the Squeeze variant targets
applications.quote: which is too slow for video applications that require real-time or interactive rates.

applications.detail: the paper's stated payoff is making keypoint-based detection usable where processing efficiency matters
applications.quote: Together these contributions for the first time reveal the potential of keypoint-based detection to be useful for applications requiring processing efficiency.

deploymentClaims: CornerNet-Squeeze runs at 34.4% AP at 30ms, real-time on the test machine
CornerNet-Saccade runs at 43.2% AP at 190ms, a 6.0x speed-up over CornerNet
All detectors timed on the same machine with a 1080Ti GPU and an Intel Core i7-7700k CPU
CornerNet-Saccade trains on four 1080Ti GPUs (44GB total) vs ten Titan X GPUs (120GB) for CornerNet

evidence.quote: we measure the inference times on the same machine with a 1080Ti GPU and an Intel Core i7-7700k CPU.
CornerNet-Saccade saves more than 60% GPU memory and requires only 4 GPUs to train, while it outperforms CornerNet.
